{{short description|American computer scientist}}
'''Oren Patashnik''' (born 1954)<ref>{{citation|url=https://viaf.org/viaf/84495586|title=Oren Patashnik|work=VIAF|access-date=2024-07-10}}</ref> is an American computer scientist. He co-created [[BibTeX]], and co-authored ''[[Concrete Mathematics|Concrete Mathematics: A Foundation for Computer Science]]''.

While working at [[Bell Labs]] in 1980, Patashnik  proved that [[Qubic]] can always be won by the first player. Using 1500 hours of computer time, Patashnik's proof is an early example of a [[computer-assisted proof]].<ref>[http://www.austms.org.au/Publ/Gazette/2005/Jul05/mathellaneous.pdf (PDF) "How to Win at Tic-Tac-Toe" (Mathellaneous, July 2005, University of Melbourne)] - 11-page article with a section relating Patashnik's effort on Qubic</ref>

In 1985, Patashnik created the bibliography-system, [[BibTeX]], in collaboration with [[Leslie Lamport]], the creator of [[LaTeX]]. LaTeX is a system and [[programming language]] for formatting documents, which is especially designed for mathematical documents. BibTeX is a widely used bibliography-formatting tool for LaTeX.<ref>{{citation|title=Text and Math Into LaTeX|first=George|last=Gratzer|publisher=Springer Nature|year=2024|isbn=9783031552816|page=[https://books.google.com/books?id=Wo4CEQAAQBAJ&pg=PA465 465]}}</ref>
 
Patashnik assisted [[Ronald Graham]] and [[Donald Knuth]] in writing the 1988 textbook ''[[Concrete Mathematics|Concrete Mathematics: A Foundation for Computer Science]]''.<ref>{{citation|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240419114108/https://maa.org/press/maa-reviews/concrete-mathematics-a-foundation-for-computer-science|archive-date=2024-04-19|url=https://maa.org/press/maa-reviews/concrete-mathematics-a-foundation-for-computer-science|title=Review of ''Concrete Mathematics''|work=MAA Reviews|first=Alan|last=Stengel|date=November 2010}}</ref>

Patashnik became a doctoral student of [[Andrew Yao]] at [[Stanford University]], where he completed his Ph.D. in 1990.<ref>{{mathgenealogy|206614}}</ref>
